reasoning_traces.think:
The source describes a maze experiment where rats initially show mixed difficulty ordering between exit-pointing and non-exit-pointing blinds (Primitive 1: near-symmetric weights w_exit ≈ w_non-exit). Reward introduction at the exit-box induces a dramatic reweighting: non-exit entrances decrease while exit-pointing blind #3 surges (Primitive 2: exponential modulation kernel with locality at blind #3). This is a conformal rescaling of the expectation field — the reward observation multiplies the prior by a likelihood concentrated on the rewarded corridor. The text explicitly questions whether behavior reflects mnemonic expectations (memory of spatial layout) or perceptual expectations (current sensory cues) (Primitive 3: unidentified mixing coefficient α). This duality creates epistemic uncertainty: any conformal prediction set must cover both hypotheses. Finally, a separate experiment with two equal-length routes shows rats prefer the route initially pointing toward the goal (Primitive 4: tanh bias on angular deviation). The four primitives form a closed loop: spatial expectation field (prior) → reward modulation (likelihood update) → mnemonic/perceptual decomposition (epistemic structure) → directional bias (policy kernel). Failure modes: (1) reward relocation breaks kernel locality; (2) sensory degradation identifies α; (3) route length asymmetry introduces cost term; (4) pre-reward symmetry assumption fails if innate bias exists.
